body: I just fixed an issue that was causing these that was released in 1.4.15, so if you are still getting these, that's very concerning.  They are using a separate cache so you can't change this right now.  What I need to see is queries in your SQL log output that aren't getting cached; this means youd see a certain query that occurs often but always says "generated" rather than "cached".   If your test suite is open source I would gladly use that to debug this issue since we want to make sure this warning never happens as it has bigger implications for the caching system.

> Hi,
> 
> What loader are you using?
> @zzzeek is this connected to #6459 ?

It looks like the same thing but it has to be a new thing if this is still seen in 1.4.15.
I thought that  #6459 was not yet released, but it's indeed in 1.4.15.

There is also the possibility that the project happens to have a huge number of variable queries that occur within the scope of a lazy load on a certain attribute.   I'd want to see that though since I couldn't come up w a scenario for that.

So I cannot give you access because it's a private repository, but I can do whatever is needed to solve this issue, just guide me.

I am not sure if I understand correctly but I think what you mean by loader it will be this. So warning occurs when I try access relationship:

```

class ExhibitorBooth(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'exhibitor_booths'

    exhibitor_id = Column(
        Integer, ForeignKey('exhibitors.id', ondelete='cascade'),
        index=True, nullable=False, primary_key=True)

    exhibitor = relationship(
        "Exhibitor", backref=backref('booth', cascade="all, delete-orphan", uselist=False), lazy="joined")

```

so in warning I see when I do `Exhibitor.booth` warning occurs:
```
SAWarning: LRU cache size alert for loader strategy: Exhibitor.booth
    if self.booth:
```

Ok, one more thing which I observed from tests. The warning occurs only when I run more than one test, for example all tests or test_exhibitors.py file, where I have 40 tests connected to exhibitors. Warning points me to specific test but when I run it alone, there is no warning.

OK can you turn on [SQL logging](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/core/engines.html#configuring-logging) and then observe for me if you see queries related to this relationship that are emitted many times but continue to say "generated", as opposed to "cached".    Background on cache logging is at https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/core/connections.html#estimating-cache-performance-using-logging
also if you can show me for Exhibitor what relationships are there and their loader strategies as well as all relationships and loader strategies assigned to ExhibitorBooth
I might know your problem.  if you are creating a new engine on every test or every suite, that would cause this problem.    there's an issue to deal wtih this problem in #5002.
Wouldn't that reset the compilation cache at each test, never actually filling it?

the LazyLoader and SelectInLoader use their own cache that's separate from that of the engine, and any subqueryload from there will also go into that cache.    so that's why this could happen.   I generally want to just change that behavior so they just use the main cache like everyone else but I've been nervous about it.

>  so that's why this could happen

oh you mean that the main engine cache does not warn, but the loader one does because it's never cleared.
Still judging from this comment 
> The warning occurs only when I run more than one test, for example all tests or test_exhibitors.py file, where I have 40 tests connected to exhibitors.

40 tests, assuming a reasonable number of query each, should not be enough to fill the query cache. Is it 1200 by default?
for the loader strategies it's 30, since there is very little variability here.
